minor.issue: Crashed 500 when event stored with event_date=None because `event.get('event_date','')[:10]` slices None. Fixed to `(event.get('event_date') or '')[:10]`. Should be applied consistently anywhere date/optional-strings are sliced.

action_items: Audit other `event.get('event_date','')[:10]` / similar `.get(k,'')[:10]` patterns in api.py - dict.get returns None (not the default) when the key exists with a None value. Same shape may exist elsewhere and blow up in production.
Consider stricter validation: /admin/site-content PUT accepts theme values as free strings; add enum validation for 'light'|'dark'.
Order field in team is used for sort but PATCH TeamIn requires all fields including order/category - accepting partial updates would be friendlier.
critical_code_review_comments: cleanup_and_seed_site() wipes users with role in ['member','user'] on FIRST run only (guarded by absence of site_settings). This one-time destructive migration is correct-but-scary; if the site_settings doc is ever manually deleted, all members/registrations will be wiped again. Consider a dedicated `migrations` collection flag instead.
server.py still contains the old seed_content() function - dead code that is never called. Remove to prevent accidental re-invocation.
core.py get_current_user still reads cookie 'access_token' but login sets no cookie (dead code path from iteration 1 - carried forward).

This may be by design (no reg needed), but confirm.
SiteContentIn allows theme any string (no enum) and admin/site-content PUT does not validate URLs in home_carousel - a malicious/typo'd string would break the hero.
TeamIn PATCH endpoint uses full model - partial updates require sending name/role again.

rca of the issue: TypeError on event registration: `dict.get(key, default)` returns the default ONLY when the key is missing. If key exists and is None, it returns None. `event.get('event_date','')[:10]` therefore raised TypeError on any event created via /admin/events without event_date (which is Optional). Fix: `(event.get('event_date') or '')[:10]`. Same idiom may exist in other f-strings in api.py.
